group: NS RRset present – returns a copy

cases.expected: RRset instance that is equal (contains the same Records) to the Zone's internal nsRRset but is not the same object (different reference). Modifying the returned RRset does not affect the Zone's internal nsRRset.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add an NS RRset containing one or more Name Server records via addRRset/addRecord, then invoke getNS(). Verify that the returned RRset contains the same records as the one added, that it is a distinct object (original != returned), and that changes to the returned RRset (e.g., adding a Record) do not reflect in the Zone's internal nsRRset.

group: NS RRset absent – returns empty RRset

cases.expected: RRset instance that is empty (size == 0) and does not throw an exception.
cases.description: Create a fresh Zone without adding any NS records. Call getNS(). The method should safely handle a null internal nsRRset and return an empty RRset rather than throwing a NullPointerException.

cases.expected: The method completes without deadlock and returns the expected RRset (as in the first two groups).
cases.description: Spawn multiple threads that concurrently invoke getNS() on the same Zone instance (both when nsRRset is set and when it is null). Verify that all calls return correct RRset objects and no thread experiences a deadlock or inconsistent state, confirming that withReadLock correctly acquires a read lock.

group: Multiple NS records – returns full copy

cases.expected: RRset instance containing all NS records that were added to the Zone, equal in content to the internal nsRRset, distinct object reference, and size matches the number of added NS records.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add three different NS records (e.g., ns1.example.com, ns2.example.com, ns3.example.com) via addRecord or addRRset. Call getNS() and verify that the returned RRset holds exactly three records, that it equals the internal nsRRset in terms of records, and that it is a different object (original != returned).

group: NS RRset removed – returns empty RRset

cases.expected: RRset instance that is empty (size == 0) after the NS RRset has been removed from the Zone.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add an NS RRset, then remove it using removeRRset(Name, Type.NS). Invoke getNS() and verify that the returned RRset is empty and no exception is thrown.

group: Modification of internal nsRRset after getNS does not affect previous copy

cases.expected: Two RRset instances: the first returned by the initial getNS() remains unchanged after the internal nsRRset is later modified; the second getNS() reflects the updated internal state.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add a single NS record, call getNS() (firstCopy). Then add another NS record directly to the Zone (e.g., via addRecord). Call getNS() again (secondCopy). Verify that firstCopy still contains only the original record while secondCopy contains both records, demonstrating that each call returns a snapshot copy.

cases.expected: After serializing and deserializing the Zone, getNS() returns an RRset equal to the original NS RRset (or empty if none were added) and is a distinct object.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add an NS RRset, serialize the Zone to a byte array, deserialize it back to a new Zone instance, then call getNS(). Verify that the returned RRset contains the same NS records as before serialization and that it is a new object.

group: Concurrent modification while reading – getNS returns a consistent snapshot

cases.expected: All concurrent calls to getNS() return RRset instances that are internally consistent (no partially‑added records) and either reflect the state before or after the concurrent add/remove operation, but never a corrupted mix.
cases.description: Start a thread that continuously adds NS records to a Zone with a short pause between each add. Simultaneously start multiple threads that repeatedly invoke getNS(). Collect the returned RRset sizes; they should be either the previous size or the new size, never an intermediate size that would indicate a partially constructed RRset.

group: Re‑entrancy of withReadLock – getNS called inside another read‑locked operation

cases.expected: getNS() completes successfully without deadlock and returns the expected RRset.
cases.description: Create a Zone with an NS RRset. Invoke withReadLock on the Zone (using reflection or a helper method) and, inside the supplied lambda, call getNS(). Verify that the method returns the correct copy of the NS RRset and no deadlock occurs, confirming that the read lock is re‑entrant for the same thread.

group: Zone contains other RRsets but no NS – getNS returns empty RRset

cases.expected: RRset instance that is empty (size == 0) while other RRsets (e.g., A, MX) exist in the Zone.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add an A record and an MX record using addRecord, but do not add any NS records. Call getNS() and verify that the returned RRset is empty and that the presence of other RRsets does not affect the result.

group: Adding a non‑NS record does not affect getNS output

cases.expected: RRset returned by getNS() remains empty (or unchanged) after adding records of other types.
cases.description: Create a fresh Zone, add a TXT record via addRecord, then call getNS(). Verify that the returned RRset is empty, demonstrating that getNS() only reflects NS records.
